findings.title: Use a patterned image to verify single sampling
findings.why_it_matters: A second resize or interpolation pass in the CLI would blur real photos while this acceptance test still passes: every source pixel is 173, so any number of resampling passes produce the same image. The change explicitly promises one sample of the original RGB image. A patterned fixture compared with the direct renderer output would make that promise observable in the CLI test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a nonuniform RGB fixture with sharp edges to the CLI test, and compare both saved outputs pixel-for-pixel with direct render_lens_float/render_lens_fixed calls using the exported effective H; retain the uniform and black fixtures for border semantics.
evidence: python/brect/lens_cli.py:83-85 -- outputs are rendered from the original image, the boundary where an added pass would affect CLI behavior

testing_gaps: The new wrapper testbench drives only coordinates listed by the generator, and that generator selects the full perimeter plus a 19x33 interior grid; the full 1920x1080 RTL mapping is modeled on the host, not simulated exhaustively. The documentation states this limit accurately.
